subject: Information Theory
title: Chain Rule for Entropy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Chain Rule for Entropy.

hook.text: How much entropy do two dice have together? You can break it into one die plus the other given the first.

buildup.text: Chain rule: H(X,Y) = H(X) + H(Y|X). Joint entropy equals marginal plus conditional.

discovery.text: For independent dice: H(X,Y) = H(X) + H(Y). The conditional adds nothing because they don't interact.

twist.text: For correlated variables, H(Y|X) < H(Y), so the joint is less than the sum. Correlation reduces total entropy.

climax.text: The chain rule extends to any number of variables, decomposing complex joint entropy step by step.

punchline.text: Joint entropy splits into what you know and what's left.

quiz.question: What does the chain rule for entropy state?
